original_test_intent: Validate the exact CPU motherboard assembly against the applicable CPU vendor's approved platform-validation plan, including correct board/CPU population, topology, firmware, interfaces and RAS/health behavior, rather than treating basic CPU recognition as full motherboard qualification.
original_method: Bind board manufacturer/product/serial/revision, CPU model/stepping/socket population, BIOS/BMC/microcode and expected NUMA, core/thread, memory-channel, UPI/inter-socket and PCIe topology; obtain the vendor plan with required passive and active checks, versions, workloads, durations and quantitative acceptance; preserve a complete inventory and health baseline; run only reviewed vendor steps with separate approval for stress, BIOS/firmware or physical actions; collect raw results and discrepancy mapping to every vendor requirement.
manual_activity: CPU vendor and platform owner identify the applicable validation plan and acceptance; an operator performs any required visual inspection or physical population check and authorizes state-changing tests separately.
required_inputs: CPU vendor validation guide/tool revision applicable to the exact motherboard, CPU family/stepping and firmware stack
Expected board/CPU/socket/core/thread/NUMA/memory/UPI/PCIe identities and topology plus BIOS/BMC/microcode matrix
Vendor-defined test list, parameters, duration, quantitative criteria and artifact format
Safety classification, approval and recovery for any stress, BIOS/firmware change, reset or physical inspection
safety_requirements: Use trusted authenticated access and preserve DMI, RAS, kernel and BMC evidence
Perform only read-only inventory until vendor active steps and their risks are reviewed
Do not infer motherboard acceptance from CPU presence or accelerator enumeration
Stop on identity/topology mismatch, missing socket/device, firmware incompatibility, RAS error, thermal/power fault or incomplete vendor artifacts
No automatic retry of vendor stress or state-changing actions
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete secure board/CPU/firmware/topology and health baseline
Map vendor requirements to executable checks and identify each separate approval boundary
Run only supplied and approved read-only or active validation steps and return raw evidence
Do not truncate to grep summaries, alter BIOS/firmware, invent criteria or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Provide the authoritative vendor guide/tool and exact platform identity/compatibility matrix
Approve the required scope, parameters, criteria and any active or physical steps with recovery
Review the requirement-by-requirement evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: lscpu, dmidecode and lspci are useful baseline inputs but the proposed grep set omits most motherboard validation domains and cannot implement unspecified CPU-vendor guidance.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: First capture complete unfiltered platform inventory and RAS/health evidence over trusted access, then execute only the exact vendor-plan checks supplied for the pinned board, CPU and firmware revision.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CPU motherboard validation by vendor guidance, no bundle, and 60/60-minute allocation remain; the absent vendor workload and acceptance scope are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a traceability matrix from each vendor requirement to stable hardware identity, exact command or physical step, raw artifact and quantitative oracle before claiming coverage.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact board/CPU/firmware binding, full platform domains, requirement-level traceability, risk separation and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: CPU model/socket/core output proves enumeration only; it cannot demonstrate board revision compatibility, memory/UPI/NUMA/PCIe topology, RAS behavior or vendor qualification.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The source delegates scope entirely to the vendor, so execution risk and coverage remain unknown until the guide is supplied; some vendor tests may be stressful or state-changing.

project_override_considerations: A project-owned validation plan may substitute only with CPU-vendor approval and an explicit mapping of every required vendor checkpoint. Generic Linux inventory, accelerator enumeration or POST success alone is insufficient.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, vendor guide/tool revision and owner approval
Board manufacturer/product/serial/revision, CPU model/stepping/socket map, BIOS/BMC/microcode and complete DMI/SMBIOS evidence
Expected versus observed core/thread/NUMA/memory-channel/UPI/PCIe topology and firmware compatibility matrix
Raw vendor-test outputs with exact parameters, duration and requirement-by-requirement acceptance
Kernel/RAS/MCE/EDAC, dmesg/journal, BMC/SEL, thermal/power and any recovery evidence
Vendor/engineer PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED decision

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria both defer to CPU-vendor guidance, so the source is consistently incomplete rather than contradictory. DeepSeek's generic inventory is supplemental only and does not redefine the target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The high-level target is CPU motherboard vendor validation. The authoritative guide and acceptance matrix are expected supplyable dependencies, so the static review can complete as pending rather than intrinsically BLOCKED.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2151 Wistron-HGX NV PVP HW-00028-V002: provide the authoritative CPU-vendor validation guide/tool revision for the exact motherboard manufacturer/product/revision and CPU model/stepping/socket population; approve BIOS/BMC/microcode, core/thread/NUMA/memory/UPI/PCIe expectations, required passive/active/physical steps, parameters/duration/acceptance, safety gates, and recovery.

review_improvement: Prevents a minimal CPU inventory from being misrepresented as vendor motherboard qualification and establishes exact platform binding and requirement-level evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A motherboard can enumerate every CPU while still violating vendor rules for stepping mix, socket population, memory channels, UPI links, firmware or RAS configuration. Because the source explicitly delegates both procedure and criteria, those rules cannot be inferred from Linux inventory. The safe review boundary is to collect a complete baseline, require the applicable vendor contract, and gate each active test independently rather than inventing a generic substitute.
